scale: delivery-plan.md: fixed 100-point planning rubric, not measured coverage
note: Coarse items are not closed by passing a limited corpus. No completion percentage is published.

items.note: String and bytes search have differential regressions. Library-produced match/capture/split iterators clone independently; language integrations and resource behavior remain partial.
The original capture differential is restored and runs alongside capture configuration checks. Native tests cover independent iterator cursors and retained results.
Replacement, split and splitN run in the full suite; cloned iterators have independent cursors. No claim of all language integrations or allocation equivalence.
RegexSet matching and SetMatches iteration exist. The full builder matrix is not closed.
The size-limit and nest-limit leaf is A5a and is already accepted. These remaining 2 points are the rest of the resource and language-integration contract.

Locked 1-point leaf: size-limit pass/fail, including a limit of 0, matches on the limit corpus, and nest-limit acceptance plus the underlined span match on 30 patterns. Re-run this turn: 60 limit checks and the syntax differential.
HIR nodes, class operations, and the tested properties exist. memory_usage is not claimed.
AST parse no longer runs the matcher first. Class items carry spans and literal kinds for the differential corpus. The corpus is not every AST field.
translate honors utf8. (?-u:\xFF), (?-u:.), (?-u:\D), and unknown properties fail at translation. The full translator is not closed.
AST and HIR display were compared on the corpus. walk and walkUntil exist. The upstream visitor trait is not fully audited.

Default prefix and suffix extraction matches regex-syntax on 32 patterns. LiteralLimits configures class, repeat, literal length, and total; seven non-default settings match Extractor. Public UTF-8 sequences match Utf8Sequences debug text. LiteralSeq cross, union, union-into-empty, keep, minimize-by-preference, reverse, sort, dedup, and longest common prefix/suffix, and prefix/suffix optimization match Seq on 66 operations. Sixteen patterns were checked so extracted prefixes and suffixes still explain every real match (38 spans). optimize_for_prefix_by_preference and optimize_for_suffix_by_preference match Seq, including the samantha/sam example, an empty literal becoming infinite, and a rare leading byte collapsed to one byte. A limited corpus does not close the item.

SearchInput carries string or bytes, a span, anchoring, selected pattern and earliest. Valid UTF-8 uses the scalar graph; invalid UTF-8 uses the shared byte compiler. Original UTF-8 pattern restrictions remain.

ThompsonNfa is a public one-graph NFA: each pattern has its own Accept, and PikeVM searches the priority union. State ids are local. There is no Rust graph-equality oracle and no separate configuration-error matrix, so the 3 points stay open.

Reverse search walks bytes backward and returns a pattern id and start. Span and end anchoring are supported; selecting a pattern requires explicit pattern-start configuration. Captures are omitted; this byte graph is separate from the scalar ThompsonNfa.
Forward search with a range and an anchor exists.

Multiple patterns share a ThompsonNfa priority union. SearchInput supports selected-pattern anchoring and unknown ids as misses. Invalid UTF-8 haystacks use a byte graph, with separate byte differential cases.

PikeCache reuses visited arrays and capture slot rows and records active state ids. This is not the original memory layout or bounded-workspace guarantee; byte search currently uses a different workspace path.
whichOverlapping reports matching pattern ids under MatchKind::All, not all spans. Range, anchor and earliest have direct Pike oracle cases. Pike has no quit-byte contract.
Earliest has direct original PikeVM differential cases. Broader configuration equivalence remains partial; quit bytes are not part of the original PikeVM contract.
The locked capture-metadata and SetMatches leaf is C4a and is already accepted. These remaining 3 points are the rest of the shared result-type contract.

Locked 2-point leaf: capturesLen, staticCapturesLen, and captureNames match string and bytes regexes on 21 patterns, and SetMatches next/nextBack/clone/sizeHint match inside the 2414 API contracts. Re-run this turn.

Multi-pattern dense/sparse search, byte input, optional pattern starts, quit and overlapping half-matches are tested. Span-end assertions inspect outside context. Sparse drops dense transitions; budgets count local slots, not original byte-layout limits.

HybridDfa builds transitions while searching. Eight searches and two reset-and-search pairs match hybrid::regex::Regex spans, including quit bytes and the lazy Unicode-word-boundary build error. A cache smaller than the seeded states is rejected. clearLimit 0 gives up with gave up searching at offset. The capacity is a state count, not upstream's byte cache, and the give-up offset is not the upstream offset. dfaSizeLimit is still the string step cache. These 4 points stay open.

OnePass is a conservative eligibility adapter executing anchored PikeVM, not a one-pass engine. Some valid original patterns are rejected by the local byte-graph check. No engine parity or performance credit.
Local memoryUsage and prefix optimizations exist; original layout, prefilter and budget contracts are not fully equivalent. Non-overlapping iteration is tracked separately under D4a.

Non-overlapping BoundedBacktracker matches use the same Searcher advance as regex-automata, including empty matches, multiple patterns, and a haystack that is too long for the visited budget. 18 iteration commands and the existing 42 searches plus 9 input queries matched this turn.
MetaRegex selects anchored Pike adaptation, HybridDfa or PikeVM and retains captures. This is not the complete original meta optimizer or strategy set.
CJD1 replays patterns and checks state count for default search configurations. Nondefault semantic configurations reject export. Not the original automata wire format.
Partial LiteRegex and CLI protocols exist. Rure is a Cangjie wrapper only; no C ABI. File input, CLI options, syntax/error parity and remaining product contracts are incomplete.

Locked 1-point leaf: find match pikevm prints pattern:start:end:escaped-text and uses exit status 0 or 1. Twenty commands match, including multiple patterns, empty matches, and syntax errors. Timing tables stay outside this point.

selected_subsets.A5: Accepted as A5a (1 point): size-limit and nest-limit rejection, including caret spans. The other 2 points stay on A5.
selected_subsets.C4: Accepted as C4a (2 points): capture metadata and SetMatches bidirectional iteration. The other 3 points stay on C4. Input and Pike captures under C1/C3 are not scored again.
selected_subsets.E: Accepted as E1 (1 point): find match pikevm span text and exit status. The demo CLI does not count. The other 9 points stay on E.
